subject: The enlightenment and the first sermon
place: Bodh Gaya (the Bodhi tree), then Sarnath (the Deer Park)
events: The prince sits beneath the Bodhi tree and endures the assault of Mara
He sees the truth of impermanence, no-self, and the cause of suffering
As the morning star rises, he becomes the Buddha
At Sarnath he sets the wheel of dharma in motion
grounding_notes: The awakening came as a dawn, not a thunderclap.
Mara is desire, fear, doubt, and delusion.
The four noble truths diagnose suffering and prescribe the cure.
The eightfold path is the way to the end of suffering.
contemporary_mapping: The modern sense of a separate, isolated self — the realization that the self is not separate from the whole.

included_characters.role_in_chapter: Protagonist — the prince who becomes the Buddha
The tempter — desire, fear, and delusion
The first disciples who hear the first sermon

chapter_summary: Beneath the Bodhi tree the prince endures the assault of Mara — desire, fear, doubt, and the armies of delusion — and does not move. In the deep watches of the night he sees the truth of all things: that all is impermanent, that all is without a fixed self, and that suffering arises from craving and clinging. As the morning star rises, he becomes the Buddha, the Awakened One. He goes to the Deer Park at Sarnath and sets the wheel of dharma in motion, teaching the four noble truths and the eightfold path. The five companions become his first disciples, and the teaching begins to spread.
